organic.title: The Thomas-Kilmann Conflict Model, explained - BiteSize Learning
organic.snippet: Understand how the Thomas-Kilmann Conflict Mode Instrument reveals five 'modes' of dealing with conflict: accommodating, avoiding, compromising, collaborating and competing. See how the two axes of cooperation and assertiveness combine in a diagram, and where each conflict mode sits.

organic.title: Thomas-Kilmann Conflict Mode Instrument (TKI - The Myers-Briggs
organic.snippet: The instrument provides detailed information about how that individual can use the five different modes, or styles – competing, collaborating, compromising, avoiding and accommodating – effectively. The TKI ® model demonstrates that these different behaviours are neither good nor bad but simply different ways of dealing with conflict.

organic.title: Conflict Styles: From Avoidance to Collaboration
organic.snippet: Stuck in a protracted conflict? A better understanding of common conflict styles, based on the Thomas-Kilmann Conflict Mode Instrument, could lead to a breakthrough.

organic.title: Module: Conflict Modes and how to use them
organic.snippet: • This model suggests there are five different ways that people tend to deal with conflict – avoiding, accommodating, competing, compromising and collaborating.

organic.title: TKI® Assessment - Thomas-Kilmann Conflict Management Tool ...
organic.snippet: It all starts with the Thomas-Kilmann Conflict Mode Instrument (TKI®), a powerful tool for understanding and managing conflict. The TKI framework identifies five possible conflict-handling modes people use in conflict situations: competing, accommodating, avoiding, collaborating, and compromising.
